title: solve an equation?
summary: Use equivalent operations, inverse operations, and careful rearranging to solve equations.

blocks.body: An equation says that two expressions have the same value. To keep it true, perform the same operation on both sides. The phrase 'move a term across the equal sign' is a shortcut for adding, subtracting, multiplying, or dividing both sides by the same suitable value.

When a term is added on one side, subtract it from both sides to undo the addition. When a term is subtracted, add it to both sides. This is why the sign appears to change when the term is moved across.
You may swap the entire left and right sides without changing any signs, because equality works in either direction. Swapping sides is different from moving one term across.
You can multiply both sides of an equation by -1. This changes every term's sign on both sides, but keeps the same solutions. Distribute -1 to every term; do not change only one term.
If the unknown is multiplied by a nonzero number, divide both sides by that number to undo the multiplication. In the shortcut language, the factor moves across as a divisor.

A useful goal for a linear equation is to collect all terms containing x on the left and all number-only terms on the right. Use addition or subtraction to collect terms, then divide by the coefficient of x.
If x is in a denominator, multiply both sides by the denominator to clear it. The denominator cannot be zero, so keep that restriction in mind. Then solve the resulting equation as usual.

You can also take the reciprocal of both sides when both sides are nonzero. For a fraction equation, this can move a denominator containing x to the numerator. Check the result in the original equation.

blocks.title: Try it
blocks.body: Solve 5x - 7 = 18. Then solve 3/x = 1/4 by taking the reciprocal of both sides, and check your answer in the original equation.
